attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; boundary refinement of claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast and claim.law.pointer-walk-array-index-regression - applies when 2+ NEARBY fields (not just one) are read/written off the same walked or index-computed base pointer within one loop iteration or straight-line block.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast's counter-form (declare one typed alias per iteration, e.g. `T* p = base + i;`, then use `p->field` at every site) is proven safe for a walked loop touching ONE field per iteration, but does NOT extend to a walked/indexed base where 3+ NEARBY fields are read together: introducing the typed alias there can defeat MWCC's combined index-register addressing (lwzx/lfsx with a register operand that already sums a strength-reduced i*stride accumulator plus a per-field byte offset) and/or its single pre-folded pointer-plus-immediate-displacement construction, forcing a real regression even though the alias is declared once and used idiomatically. Three independent confirmations, the third establishing this is NOT limited to per-iteration loop accumulators: (1) WorldSaveInitState's per-object snapshot loop reads WorldObj.parent and .pos[0..2] (4 fields) off `*wobjsp + i*60`; a typed `WorldObj* wo = *wobjsp + i;` regressed real 64->68. (2) WorldPsysActivate reads coltri.pos[0..2] (3 fields) off `ctris_base + ctriidx*40 + 8`; a typed `struct coltri* ctri = ...; ctri->pos[k]` regressed real 0->21. (3) SetItem (items.c): `wobj = (u8*)gWorldInfo.wobjs + wobj_index*0x3C` is computed ONCE, outside any loop, then held across a straight-line block touching 3 distinct nearby fields (flags@0x10, byte@0x16, byte@0x17); BOTH a repeated inline `(WorldObj*)wobj` cast at just the one remaining raw write AND a declared-once `WorldObj* wtarget` alias regressed real 528->739, even though the identical typed-cast form was already neutral at the OTHER 3 flags sites in the same function -- meaning the failure is not simply 'typed casts on this field are unsafe' but specifically the combination of a 3rd near-field touch off an index-computed base under SetItem's extreme (1306-insn) register pressure. In all three cases the verified-safe form is the RAW walked/indexed pointer with offsetof-computed (not bare-hex) displacements per field - i.e. claim.law.offsetof-fused-immediate-counter's form, never a typed intermediate - even where the field count is small enough that a typed alias looks like the more natural/idiomatic C, and even when the base pointer is computed only once rather than re-derived every loop iteration. Rule of thumb going forward: A/B a typed alias against the raw offsetof form whenever a walked OR index-computed pointer (loop-iterated or one-shot) feeds MORE THAN ONE field access within the same block; do not assume a single-field or low-register-pressure precedent transfers, especially inside very large (1000+ insn) functions.
